title: Assessing Judging Bias in Large Reasoning Models: An Empirical Study

bias_targets.methodology: Modifying original evaluation samples by inserting statements that falsely attribute incorrect answers to majority opinion (e.g., '90% of people believe option A is better').
Injecting fabricated citations or endorsements from fictional experts to lend false credibility and unwarranted weight to incorrect answers.
Systematically altering the order of answer options (e.g., alternating between positions A and B) to isolate the effect of placement on model selection.
Introducing tangentially related but ultimately irrelevant information to a prompt to evaluate if it derails the model's reasoning process.
Inserting phrases that mimic human deliberation (e.g., 'wait, let me think about it') between options to measure artificial preference shifts toward options in later positions.
